name: Speex
listed_description: A free codec for free speech. Obsoleted by Opus.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline. README, NEWS, OPTIMIZE (to-do notes only) and doc/manual.lyx (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) give only the project's own complexity figures (about 0.5 mflops decode, encoder complexity 10 about 5x the CPU of complexity 1, fixed-point vs floating-point advice) and no comparison with GSM-FR, G.729, Opus or any other codec. speex.org itself is blocked here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). The speexdsp resampler is a separate repo and was not examined.

name: TagLib
listed_description: A library for reading and editing the metadata of several popular audio formats.
reason: Directional only. README and CHANGELOG (opened) contain no benchmark; the CHANGELOG says only 'Speed up Matroska reading by using seek head' and 'smaller bug fixes and performance improvements' with no numbers. Navidrome docs (WebSearch snippet only, page not opened) say TagLib is faster than the ffmpeg extractor, without numbers. A 2007 taglib-devel mailing-list post (snippet only, mail.kde.org blocked here) reportedly shows TagLib importing 15721 files in 380 s vs libid3tag 15718 files in 432 s, but it cannot be opened and is 19 years old, so no record. lofty-rs README (opened) points to cargo bench with no TagLib comparison.

name: Theora
listed_description: A free and open video compression format.
reason: No opened page carries a number against a named baseline. README and CHANGES (opened) say only 'better performance' and 'speed improvements' for 1.1/1.2 versus earlier libtheora, with no figures. Third-party numbers exist only as unopened WebSearch snippets from blocked hosts (ffmpeg-devel 2009-July/069729 and 069730 reportedly say libtheora is about 30% faster than ffmpeg's native Theora decoder only at HD sizes and on ARM11; a 2005 doom9 thread has libtheora alpha4 at 71 fps vs libavcodec 86.7 fps; a Big Buck Bunny 1080p timing reportedly has libtheora 1.1 at 4:51 vs ffmpeg 6:09 with two threads), so the result is mixed and cannot be verified here. Leads if egress opens: https://ffmpeg.org/pipermail/ffmpeg-devel/2009-July/069729.html and https://multimedia.cx/eggs/?p=1867.

name: TinyDNG
listed_description: Header-only Tiny DNG/TIFF loader and writer in C++.
reason: Only comparisons against its own earlier code. benchmark/ljpeg92-v2 and benchmark/streamwrite READMEs (opened) compare scalar/SSE2/AVX2 builds of tiny_dng_ljpeg92_v2 and report encode MPix/s on a Threadripper 1950X with gcc -O2; sandbox/lj92/README.md (opened) reports a rewritten lj92 codec at 99.3 MPix/s decode vs 61.4 for the project's own 'v2 (ref)' and 41.4 vs 18.8 MPix/s encode (gcc 13.3, Threadripper 1950X, -O3), and commit 51d2d38 says 'about 1.5x faster' than the pre-port code. The 'v2' reference is TinyDNG's own previous codec, not libtiff, LibRaw, dcraw or liblj92 as shipped, and the README (rewritten as a pure C11 v3 API, no longer header-only C++) has no comparison with them. Revisit if v2 is accepted as a liblj92 derivative.

name: TinyEXIF
listed_description: Tiny ISO-compliant C++ EXIF and XMP parsing library for JPEG.
reason: No performance claim at all. README and CHANGELOG (opened) mention only 'tiny, lightweight' and fuzz-hardening; the only 'speed' hits are drone flight-speed fields. No benchmark directory (Samples, fuzz, cmake only). WebSearch for TinyEXIF vs exiv2 or libexif speed found nothing.

name: TinySpline
listed_description: A small, yet powerful ANSI C library for interpolating, transforming, and querying arbitrary NURBS, B-Splines, and Bézier curves
reason: No benchmark or speed claim. README (opened) lists features only; repo has no benchmark directory (docs, examples, res, src, test, tools); issue search for performance/benchmark/faster returned two unrelated issues (#235, #138). The SANER 2021 paper (see.uni-bremen.de) and a 2026 comparison guide (pistack.xyz) are blocked here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND); WebSearch snippets of both show feature comparison only, no timings.
